name: Grid
summary: Lays out children in columns and rows: a fixed column count, or as many columns as fit at a minimum item size.
useWhen: Cards, files or tiles of the same kind that line up in columns and rows
A form or settings page with two or three columns on wide screens and one on phones
A twelve column page layout where some cells span more columns
avoidWhen: Items in one line or one column only
Tiles of deliberately mixed sizes on an overview or landing section
Tabular data a person compares across rows
A visual order that differs from the reading order

columns.description: A number from 1 to 12 gives equal tracks. auto-fit fits as many columns as minItemSize allows and grows them to fill the row. Fixed counts fall to one column under breakpoint.phone unless keepColumns is set. Sets data-columns.

minItemSize.description: The smallest item width with auto-fit: sm 10rem, md 15rem, lg 24rem, derived from the breakpoint tokens until a size.grid scale exists. Capped at 100% of the grid, so one item never overflows at 320px. Sets data-min.

gap.description: Space between cells on both axes, a space.* step.

rowGap.description: Space between rows when it differs from gap.

keepColumns.description: Keeps a fixed column count on phones. Sets data-keep-columns. Only for short cells, such as a calendar or a keypad.

as.description: The element to render. ul and ol get role list and lose their bullets; use GridItem as li inside.

GridItem.span.description: Columns the item spans; full spans the whole row. Sets data-span. On phones every item fills the one column.

GridItem.rowSpan.description: Rows the item spans. Sets data-row-span.

GridItem.as.description: The element of the item. li inside a list Grid.

children.description: The cells, plain elements or GridItem.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div, or list on ul and ol
a11y.focus: Never focusable. Focus and reading order are the DOM order: cells fill from the start side, the right in Arabic.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Grid is layout only.
notes: This is a layout grid, not role grid. A grid of interactive cells with arrow key navigation is a different component (DataGrid).
No dense packing and no order property: the visual order must match the DOM order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
One column under breakpoint.phone and capped track minimums keep the page free of sideways scroll at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10).

en.items: No copy of its own. Cells carry their own labels.

ar.items: No copy of its own. Cells fill from the right in Arabic because the tracks follow dir.

react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies. The phone fallback is a viewport media query; a Grid in a narrow sidebar on a wide screen keeps its columns, so use auto-fit there.

angular.note: The host element is the root and the item, so as is not needed.

native.note: No CSS grid in React Native: fixed columns map to a percentage basis per item and auto-fit to a basis from onLayout width.

styles.studio: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.desk: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.neutral: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.liquid: Layout only. The gap follows density.

mistakes.wrong: columns 4 with fixed pixel widths on each cell
mistakes.right: columns 4, or auto-fit with minItemSize, so tracks shrink and fall to one column on phones

mistakes.wrong: A GridItem span larger than an auto-fit grid has tracks
mistakes.right: span full, or a fixed column count, since auto-fit has fewer tracks on narrow screens

mistakes.wrong: keepColumns on a grid of cards with text
mistakes.right: Leave the phone fallback on; keepColumns is for short cells like a keypad

mistakes.wrong: role grid on a layout Grid
mistakes.right: No role; arrow key navigation between cells belongs to DataGrid
